description:
Early exit polls from Israel's election project 24 seats for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and 22 for Gadi Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party. Itamar Ben-Gvir's far-right Otzma Yehudit and Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionism are each projected to win six seats, while the Palestinian-led Joint List could secure 11 seats and the United Arab List, or Ra'am, seven.
Marwan Bishara, Al Jazeera's senior political analyst, says that although Likud is projected to emerge as the largest party, the opposition bloc appears to have more seats than Netanyahu's governing coalition, creating a political paradox. He explains that President Isaac Herzog will have to consult political parties to determine who has the best chance of forming a government, rather than automatically choosing the leader of the largest party. The first minister of Wales says his nation deserves a new deal from the United Kingdom. Rhun ap Iorwerth says its relationship with the UK is not working because the union is not one of equals. That is why he is pushing for an agreement that will fix what he calls "historic unfairness".

In a letter to the British prime minister, the Welsh first minister has formally requested the transfer of more power to Wales to allow it to control its policing, justice system, rail network and natural resources. His centre-left Welsh nationalist party, Plaid Cymru, came to power in May, ending more than a century of Labour Party dominance in Wales. Just four months into his term, he signed a pact with Scotland and Northern Ireland declaring their right to self-determination, and warning the British Parliament that its time is coming to an end.
